Fibrillary Glomerulonephritis: Electron microscopy of a single glomerulus: numerous fibrils with a diameter of 10.6–13.8 nm and within an expanded mesangial matrix
Immunofluorescence: diffuse patchy granular mesangial and peripheral IgG (2+), C3 (+), and IgM (+)

top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient presents with haematuria, proteinuria, and declining renal function, which are all consistent with Fibrillary Glomerulonephritis. Electron microscopy and immunofluorescence results also support this diagnosis.

The patient has a history of antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, which can cause renal dysfunction, haematuria, and proteinuria. However, the presence of fibrils in glomeruli and mesangial matrix increase are more specific to Fibrillary Glomerulonephritis.
